title: Preventing Grease Accumulation in Kitchen P-Traps
description: Fats, oils, and grease enter kitchen drains as hot liquids, but as they travel into the cool P-trap and drainage branch, they rapidly lose heat. This temperature drop causes grease to solidify and adhere to the inner pipe walls, gradually restricting wastewater flow. Running cold water while washing greasy cookware speeds up this solidification inside the trap. To maintain clear drainage, scrape heavy grease from pots and plates into the trash before washing, and follow dishwashing with a warm water flush to carry suspended fats past the trap seal into the main drain line. How do you prevent grease buildup in your sink?

Clean, professional background, realistic plumbing geometry, photorealistic render, no text, no labels, no watermark, no logos.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear cutaway view of a kitchen P-trap beneath a sink basin to show the hidden interior mechanics of drain restricted flow. Viewers will observe how melted fats don't simply wash away; instead, they cling to the cold inner walls of the PVC trap curve, forming a thick deposit that narrows the path for wastewater. This directly illustrates why kitchen sinks gradually slow down over time.

on_image_text.takeaway: Scrape cookware into the trash before washing.
